name: Accuracy classes and maximum permissible errors for trade measuring instruments
description: Accuracy classes and maximum permissible errors that the law assigns to instruments used for trade, from three authorities that do not publish a common table: Directive 2014/32/EU (the EU Measuring Instruments Directive), Directive 2014/31/EU and OIML R 76-1 (non-automatic weighing instruments), and NIST Handbook 44 code 2.20 (scales, United States). Each record is one instrument type at one accuracy class under one measurement condition, with the permitted error that authority states. The MID side covers nine of the ten instrument-specific annexes: water meters (MI-001), gas meters and volume conversion devices (MI-002), thermal energy meters (MI-004), measuring systems for liquids other than water including fuel dispensers and road tankers (MI-005), automatic weighing instruments (MI-006), taximeters (MI-007), material measures (MI-008), dimensional measuring instruments (MI-009) and exhaust gas analysers (MI-010). Active electrical energy meters (MI-003) carry no records, and that is a statement about the source rather than an omission: Annex V sets its limits in a Table 2 whose load-current bands EUR-Lex renders as images, so neither the band nor the value it pairs with is in the page's text and no row can be keyed to it honestly. Annex VI is thin for the same reason -- every formula in it is an image, so only the flow sensor's 5 % cap, which the directive states in words, is here. Answers 'what is the maximum permissible error for a water meter', 'what accuracy class does a petrol pump have to be', 'MID accuracy class for a taximeter', 'allowed error on a weighbridge', 'thermal energy meter accuracy class 2 MPE', 'is a class III scale legal for trade in both the EU and the US' and 'is my fuel dispenser within tolerance'. The values are condition-dependent -- the error allowed at low flow differs from the error allowed at high flow, and in-service limits differ from new-instrument limits -- so a single percentage figure is almost always the wrong answer. The weighing records are what makes this a juxtaposition rather than a restatement: for a non-automatic weighing instrument the EU directive and OIML R 76-1 state the same three limits over the same load bands, while NIST Handbook 44 adds a fourth band to classes III and IIII and carries a class III L that exists nowhere in Europe. No single document says that, and getting it today means reading a 443,000-character standard, a 300,000-character directive and a 470,000-character handbook side by side.

records.scope_note: However, Member States may require measuring systems of accuracy class 0,3 or 0,5 when used for the levying of duties on mineral oils when (un)loading ships and rail and road tankers.
records.source_quote: 7. Putting into use Table 5 Accuracy Class | Types of Measuring system | 0,3 | Measuring systems on pipeline | 0,5 | All measuring systems if not differently stated elsewhere in this Table, in particular: — | fuel dispensers (not for liquefied gases), | — | measuring systems on road tankers for liquids of low viscosity (< 20 mPa.s) | — | measuring systems for (un)loading ships and rail and road tankers (2) | — | measuring systems for milk | — | measuring systems for refuelling aircraft | | 1,0 | Measuring systems for liquefied gases under pressure measured at a temperature equal to or above – 10 °C | Measuring systems normally in class 0,3 or 0,5 but used for liquids — | whose temperature is less than – 10 °C or greater than 50 °C | — | whose dynamic viscosity is higher than 1 000 mPa.s | — | whose maximum volumetric flowrate is not higher than 20 L/h | | 1,5 | Measuring systems for liquefied carbon dioxide | Measuring systems for liquefied gases under pressure measured at a temperature below – 10 °C (other than cryogenic liquids) | 2,5 | measuring systems for cryogenic liquids (temperature below – 153 °C) | Note: However, the manufacturer may specify a better accuracy for a certain type of measuring system.

records.measurement_condition: durability test, error of indication, Q1 to Q2 excluded
records.source_quote: The error of indication for the volume metered after the durability test shall not exceed: — | ± 6 % of the metered volume between Q1 included and Q2 excluded; | — | ± 2,5 % of the metered volume between Q2 included and Q4 included for water meters intended to meter water with a temperature between 0,1 °C and 30 °C, | — | ± 3,5 % of the metered volume between Q2 included and Q4 included for water meters intended to meter water with a temperature between 30 °C and 90 °C.
